A major challenge with the presented dataset is the fact that the A-stage processes, HR-CS included, are more complex with more parameters influencing effluent quality including settleability, bioflocculation, internal storage, and clarifier loadings (AlSayed et al. 2023). It relies on the biosorption of the slowly biodegradable carbon to biomass, and subsequent solids- liquid separation via settling in a clarifier. The former can be influenced by influent characteristics, operational conditions, and environmental conditions, while the latter can be affected by biomass characteristics, loading rates, and clarifier capacity (AlSayed et al. 2023). As a result, prior mechanistic knowledge was not used to filter out features and resulted in considering more than 120 features resulting in high dimensionality. Another challenge with the data is the high degree of missingness and inconsistency in such a missingness. As shown in Figure 5-4, data availability varies significantly from one feature to another. This challenge was multiplied with the data where sampling frequency and routine varied significantly including COVID periods. Figure 5-4. Missing Data in an Exemplary Part of the Dataset. Each Column Represents One Feature, and each Gray Bar Represents One Point of the Data. A White (Empty) Cell Indicates No Data for That Feature at That Point of Observation. 5.1.4 Prepare Data Data cleaning included elimination of selected features or time periods due to sensor malfunctions, process upsets, maintenance events, and very low variance. Following this, in Integration of Data Driven Process Control for Maximizing Energy and Resource Efficiency in WRRFs 37 coordination with DC Water research team, a thorough data quality review was performed to fix errors like negative values, typing errors, and uncommon extreme values.
